## README

 

**One brain for you and your company, read by every agent you use.** Put your own notes and your company's docs in one place: a facts page, a decisions log, call transcripts. Claude Code, Codex and your other agents look there before they answer, so they stop starting from zero and work from what you and your team actually wrote down.

GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host, and it starts with no API keys: search is by keyword until you add one. gbrain.io is optional paid hosting.

> [!TIP]
> **Need hosted? First time running an agent?** Try **gbrain.io**, hosted GBrain, for the easiest experience: one brain for you and your team, connected to ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor, with nothing to install or keep online. Stuck? Email support@gbrain.io and a person will set it up with you, free.

**A few minutes after you install it:**

- Every new Claude Code or Codex session looks in your brain before it answers, without being told to.
- Anything you ask your agent to remember is still there in the next session, in every agent connected to the brain.
- Your notes and your company's docs are searchable, and your agent answers questions like *"what did we decide about pricing, and why?"* from them.

**Works with these agents** (each name links to its guide):

| How it connects | Agents |
|---|---|
| One command wires memory, hooks and instructions | Claude Code (`gbrain setup claude-code`), Codex (`gbrain setup codex`) |
| MCP from its guide, then `gbrain setup ` adds the brain-first instructions | OpenClaw, Hermes, opencode, Cursor |
| MCP from its guide | ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Claude Cowork, Perplexity, Grok Build, Grok Bot, Muse, Windsurf and other stdio clients |
| Any other coding agent | Paste the install prompt below |

Hermes in single-query mode refuses `curl … | bash`, `bun install -g github:…` (its scanner, Tirith, can't finish a package lookup for a `github:` spec) and commands that append to a dotfile such as `~/.profile`. # Publishes a GitHub release for every VERSION bump that lands on master:
# tag + title `v<VERSION>`, notes from that version's CHANGELOG.md entry,

# for Node adapters (gbrain-skill-resolver.mjs, GBRA-377).
#
# Every release is published as a pre-release that never becomes GitHub's
# "Latest": scripts/promote-stable.ts marks the stable release Latest, with
# notes rolled up since the previous stable, so the Releases page and its
# Latest badge show the release installs follow. The alpha channel follows
# the latest-stable tag this workflow moves last; binary self-update reads
# VERSION there and downloads that exact release (src/core/binary-self-update.ts),
# never releases/latest. Bring older releases in line, or take the rule out,
# with scripts/release-channel.ts (docs/RELEASING.md).
#
# Idempotent: the `version` job skips build+release when a release for
# v<VERSION> already exists WITH all expected assets. A half-published release
# (tag exists / assets incomplete) is repaired on the next run — softprops
# updates the existing release in place. Historical 3-segment tags are never
# touched; a new 4-segment VERSION always mints a new tag.
#
# The asset names are a contract with expectedAssetName() in
# src/core/binary-self-update.ts, pinned by test/release-workflow.test.ts.
#
# CI gate (docs/RELEASING.md#release-ci-gate): the `ci-gate` job waits for
# the push-to-master runs of Test and E2E Tests on the release commit
# (scripts/release-gate.ts). Build, publication and the latest-stable move
# run only after both succeed. A failed or cancelled run publishes nothing
# and the job fails with the next step; master push runs are keyed by commit,
# so no newer push cancels them, and no later commit is published in the
# release commit's place (it may carry unreleased changes under the same
# VERSION). workflow_dispatch backfills only while master HEAD is the release
# commit (the commit that last changed VERSION); otherwise it refuses and names
# the re-run of that commit's push Release run.
#
# Releases per batch (docs/RELEASING.md#releases-per-batch): PRs land with
# changelog.d fragments and no version; a release PR moves VERSION, so this
# workflow runs once per release. Its ci-gate refuses a commit that still
# holds an unfolded fragment or a stale behavior-change table.

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
    paths: [VERSION]
  workflow_dispatch: {}  # backfill of the current VERSION while master HEAD is its release commit

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
      exists: ${{ steps.v.outputs.exists }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
      - id: v
        name: Read VERSION and check for an existing complete release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          version="$(tr -d '[:space:]' < VERSION)"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Complete = release exists AND carries every asset the self-updater
          # can request. A partial release must NOT short-circuit, so a re-run
          # can repair it.
          assets="$(gh release view "v$version" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --json assets --jq '[.assets[].name] | sort | join(",")' 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [ "$assets" = "gbrain-darwin-arm64,gbrain-linux-x64,gbrain-skill-resolver.mjs,gbrain-skill-resolver.mjs.sha256" ]; then
            echo "exists=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Release v$version already published with all assets — nothing to do."
